A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FocusLLM despite the changed title and organization. All 13 pages of v1 and 14 pages of v2, including equations, tables, figures, and appendices, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original FocusLLM language-modeling, downstream-task, retrieval, efficiency, and ablation results in Tables 2–5 and accompanying figures.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results in Tables 1–4 and adds candidate-token attention visualizations in Appendix H.

M1.justification: Chunking, local-context injection, trainable candidate-token projections, frozen decoding, and both training objectives are retained. Dynamic condensing reframes the existing mechanism, and Reconstruction Loss renames Repetition Loss. Explicit prompt-update instructions clarify inference without establishing an algorithm change.

E1.justification: Reported training coverage changes from 70K RedPajama plus 10K LongAlpaca instruction-following examples to 80K RedPajama examples (v2 Appendix B). Table 8 additionally reports a Math Calc evaluation. The principal evaluation datasets, domains, and languages remain unchanged.

E2.justification: The retained comparisons use the same methods. Although v2 newly tabulates Activation Beacon's ∞-Bench scores, v1 already includes it in that benchmark's protocol and discusses its poor results in Section 3.3; this supplies numerical evidence for an existing comparator.

E3.justification: RedPajama's reported training count increases from 70K to 80K within the unchanged 80K total. The lowest training-length bin changes from 2K–4K to 3K–4K, matching both versions' prose. Retained benchmark metrics, sample counts, and truncation procedures are unchanged; these reporting revisions do not establish reruns.

E4.justification: v2 Section 5.1 and Appendix H add attention-head case studies examining selective retrieval in Passkey Retrieval and information aggregation in NarrativeQA. Existing loss ablations, context/chunk-size analyses, efficiency measurements, and 400K-context experiments are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or comparable uncertainty estimates. The new attention heatmaps do not introduce statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v1 Tables 2–5 and v2 Tables 1–4 retain identical numerical values. New Table 8 reports Activation Beacon accuracies of 21.32 for Code Debug, 11.71 for Math Find, 0.00 for Math Calc and KV Retrieval, and 1.69 for Passkey and Number String. v2 also adds attention-pattern findings and explicit CEPE/LongLLaMA ∞-Bench memory-failure statements.

T1.justification: The attention equations and autoregressive objective retain their mathematical substance after symbol and local-token indexing changes. The complexity argument moves from v1 Section 2.1.4 to v2 Appendix A. No new theorem, proof, or substantive derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The central claims remain efficient context extension, preservation of relevant information, strong downstream performance, and operation up to 400K tokens with a 0.5B-token training budget. The new title and contribution list emphasize dynamic condensing, but largely restate claims already made in v1.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations of attention patterns as noise filtering and multi-chunk aggregation, and states that candidate tokens cannot fully replace local-context information. Its limitations discuss benefits from larger training datasets and future quantization; the hardware-imposed 400K testing limit was already disclosed. v1's explanation for rising CodeParrot perplexity is removed.

D1.justification: v2 explicitly documents updating the dynamic prompt after each generated token and optionally dropping its first token to preserve length. Conversely, v1's explicit fixed 2048-token local training context is no longer stated. Hardware, optimizer, training duration, and most hyperparameters are retained in Appendix C.

R1.justification: v2 removes v1 Appendix A's decoder-decoder/T5 comparison and synthetic-data discussion, dropping citations including Sun et al. (2024), Raffel et al. (2020), and Wu et al. (2024). The main related-work categories remain, with greater emphasis on dynamic versus fixed context compression.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, and architecture explanation are substantially rewritten around dynamic condensing. Architecture and training become separate sections, local-context analysis is merged into ablations, and efficiency, training-data statistics, and experimental details move into reorganized appendices.

P2.justification: v2 removes the standard-decoder diagram and revises the FocusLLM diagram to distinguish frozen decoders from trainable condensing components. It adds Table 8 and two 18-panel attention-heatmap figures, relocates the 400K perplexity plot to Appendix G, and rearranges existing plots, tables, and captions.

improvement.justification: v2 clarifies previously implicit prompt updates and the frozen/trainable architecture, while attention visualizations and Table 8 make existing mechanism and baseline-performance assertions more inspectable. These provide limited gains in clarity and evidential support. The core benchmark numbers remain identical, and the unexplained training-corpus revision and omitted training-context detail limit the reproducibility improvement.
